reference_formalization: ∀ (a b c : Point) (AB BC AC : Line), formTriangle a b c AB BC AC ∧ |(b─c)| * |(b─c)| = |(b─a)| * |(b─a)| + |(a─c)| * |(a─c)| → ∠ b:a:c = ∟
nl_statement: For let the square on one of the sides, $BC$, of triangle $ABC$ be equal to the (sum of the) squares on the sides $BA$ and $AC$. I say that angle $BAC$ is a right-angle. <prf>  Thus, $BAC$ is also a right-angle.Thus, if the square on one of the sides of a triangle is equal to the (sum of the) squares on the remaining two sides of the triangle then the angle contained by the remaining two sides of the triangle is a right-angle.
